conventions.convention: KL is directional: D(P||Q) is infinite when P is not absolutely continuous with respect to Q. Its log-density integral has finite negative part; zero-density logarithms are assigned zero for integration under P.
Mutual information is joint KL against the product of marginals, uses natural logarithms, and takes values in [0,+infinity].
Probability-kernel sections are probability measures at every base point, including exceptional points; event evaluations are measurable.

The same-marginal conditional-product law is written in coordinate order Z,X,Y, with rectangle mass R(C×A×B) equal to the integral over C of K(z,A)L(z,B). Kernel versions may change on a measurable conditioning-null set without changing R.
Finite-alphabet conditional entropy permits a standard-Borel observation, uses 0 ln 0 = 0, and integrates the entropy of a supplied conditional probability vector.
Law entropy means H(X)=I(X;X), an extended nonnegative quantity; it is distinct from differential entropy.
Quantizer sigma-algebras increase and generate the full coordinate sigma-algebras; conditional quantization retains the entire conditioning variable Z.
The KL and mutual-information chain rules are additive equalities of extended nonnegative quantities and do not subtract infinities.

load_bearing.statement: For probability measures P,Q on one measurable space, D(P||Q) is the supremum of ∫f dP − ln ∫exp(f) dQ over bounded measurable real f, and equivalently the supremum of the support-aware finite KL sums over finite measurable partitions. Singular and infinite-divergence cases are included.

For standard-Borel random elements X,Y,Z and supplied conditional laws K,L given Z, their product is a probability kernel. The law R(C×A×B)=∫C K(z,A)L(z,B) P_Z(dz) exists uniquely, is independent of the versions K,L, has Z marginal P_Z, and has conditional law K⊗L for (X,Y) given Z.
For standard-Borel E,F, probabilities μ,ν on E, and probability kernels K,L:E→F, if P=μ⋉K and Q=ν⋉L, then D(P||Q)=D(μ||ν)+∫D(K(x,·)||L(x,·)) μ(dx)=D(μ||ν)+D_μ(K||L), as an equality in [0,+infinity].
For probability kernels K:Z→E and L:Z→F between measurable spaces, z↦K(z,·)⊗L(z,·) is a probability kernel on the product sigma-algebra.
For probability kernels K,L from a measurable space Z into a standard-Borel space E, z↦D(K(z,·)||L(z,·)) is measurable, with +infinity allowed.
For a standard-Borel probability law P, S={x:P({x})>0} is countable. If P(S)=1 with atom masses p_i, H(X)=Σ p_i ln(1/p_i), allowing +infinity. If P(S)<1, H(X)=+infinity.

concerns.concern: The Definition introduces the joint law P_XYZ, defines R by 'R(C×A×B)=∫C K(z,A)L(z,B) P_Z(dz)', and then defines 'I(X;Y|Z):=D(P_XYZ||R)'. The rectangle formula places R on Z×X×Y, whereas P_XYZ is the joint law on X×Y×Z. For distinct value spaces these are different measurable domains, so the displayed KL is not defined as written. No coordinate-permutation convention is stated. The examples and chain-rule proof instead explicitly use P_ZXY. This defining expression needs an explicit common coordinate order.

Proof step 1.1 says 'taking C equal to the whole Z space shows its Z marginal is P_Z'. Taking C to be the whole Z space leaves the (X,Y) marginal. To obtain the Z marginal from the displayed rectangle identity, A and B must be their whole value spaces, with C arbitrary. The intended marginal assertion follows immediately.
